(SPEC §20) plus a tutorial-derived suite (T01–T12) tracking the 1-2-3
R3.1 Tutorial chapters end-to-end.

---

## ✦ Install

### Homebrew (macOS / Linux)

[Homebrew](https://brew.sh) is the standard package manager for macOS
(and works on Linux too). If you don't already have it, install it
first from [brew.sh](https://brew.sh), then:

```bash
brew install duane1024/l123/l123
```

Or tap once and install by name:

```bash
brew tap duane1024/l123
brew install l123
```

Upgrade later with `brew upgrade l123`.

### From source

Requires Rust stable (pinned via `rust-toolchain.toml`).

```bash
git clone git@github.com:duane1024/l123.git
cd l123
cargo build --release
./target/release/l123            # or: cargo run -p l123
```

Open an existing workbook:

```bash
l123 financials.xlsx
```

Inspect or initialize configuration:

```bash
l123 config            # show effective settings and their sources
l123 config --init     # write a sample ~/.l123/L123.CNF
```

See [`docs/CONFIG.md`](docs/CONFIG.md) for the full list of keys and
environment variables.

---

## ✦ Keyboard, the short version

The keyboard *is* the product.

| Key | What it does |
|---|---|
| `/` | Open the slash menu |
| `:` | Open the `:` (WYSIWYG) menu |
| First letter | Descend into a menu item (no `Enter` needed) |
| Arrows / `Tab` | Move pointer; during entry, commit-and-move |
| `Enter` | Commit cell entry |
| `Esc` | Back out one level (menu, prompt, POINT anchor) |
| `Ctrl-Break` | Abort to READY from anywhere; cancel a WAIT op |
| `.` (in POINT) | Cycle which corner of the range is anchored |
| `F1` | Context help (824-page R3.1 manual, navigable) |
| `F2` | Edit current cell |
| `F3` | List named ranges (overlay; works in GOTO and prompts) |
| `F4` | Cycle `$` absoluteness in a reference |
| `F5` | GOTO cell or named range |
| `F7` | Repeat last `/Data Query` |
| `F8` | Repeat last `/Data Table` |
| `F9` | Recalculate |
| `F10` | Full-screen graph view |
| `Alt-F2` | STEP — single-step macro execution |
| `Alt-F3` | RUN — invoke a macro by name |
| `Alt-F4` | Undo |
| `Alt-F5` | LEARN — toggle keystroke recording |
| `Alt-`*letter* | Run macro `\`*letter* (e.g. `Alt-A` → `\A`) |
| `Ctrl-PgUp` / `Ctrl-PgDn` | Previous / next sheet |
| `Ctrl-End` then `Ctrl-PgUp/PgDn` | Previous / next open file |

Mouse is supported for the WYSIWYG icon panel (17 icons, R3.4a layout)
plus cell click, drag-select, scroll wheel, and POINT extend.

Formulas use 1-2-3 syntax: `@SUM(A1..A5)`, not `=SUM(A1:A5)`. The `@`
sigil and `..` separator are required. `#AND#`, `#OR#`, `#NOT#` are the
logical operators.

First character typed in READY decides label vs. value: digits and
`+ - . ( @ # $` start a value; anything else starts a label (with an
auto-inserted `'` prefix). `"` = right-align, `^` = center, `\-` fills the
cell with dashes.

---

## ✦ What works today

**Core UX**

- Three-line control panel with live mode indicator
- 13 modes (READY, LABEL, VALUE, EDIT, POINT, MENU, FILES, NAMES, HELP,
  ERROR, WAIT, FIND, STAT)
- Full slash-menu tree: every path in `docs/MENU.md` is reachable; MVP
  leaves execute, non-MVP leaves show "Not implemented yet" in line 3
- POINT mode with `.` corner cycle, F3 named-range picker, typed
  addresses, and mouse drag-select
- Async WAIT mode for long ops (file load/save, recalc, large imports)
  with progress bar and Ctrl-Break cancellation

**Worksheet, Range, File**

- `/Worksheet`, `/Range`, `/Copy`, `/Move`, `/File`, `/Quit` —
  full menus implemented
- `.xlsx` round-trip through IronCalc (formulas, alignment, borders,
  comments, fills, fonts, frozen panes, hidden sheets, merges,
  sheet color, tables); `.csv` import and export
- `.WK3` read (values, formulas, basic styles, column widths) via the
  optional `wk3` cargo feature, gated behind a local `ironcalc_lotus`
  fork — see CLAUDE.md
- 3D workbooks: `A..IV` sheets, `A:B3..C:D5` ranges, GROUP mode
- Named ranges (Create/Delete/Reset/Labels/Note/Table/Undefine);
  `@` function set including the legacy `@D360`, `@DGET`, `@REPLACE`
- Command-journal undo (Alt-F4), toggleable via `/WGD Other Undo`
- Multi-file sessions (`/File Open Before|After`, Ctrl-End navigation,
  `/File List`)

**Print, Graph, Data**

- `/Print File` to ASCII, PDF, or line-printer output; headers, footers,
  margins, page-length, formatted / unformatted / as-displayed /
  cell-formulas modes; column page breaks; `|` in first column hides
  rows from print
- `/Range Search Formulas|Labels|Both` Find and Replace
- `/Graph` tree: Line, Bar, XY, Stack, Pie, HLCO, Mixed; Titles, Legend,
  Scale, Grid, Color/B&W, Data-Labels; Name Create/Use/Delete/Reset/Table
- F10 / `/Graph View` full-screen rendering with Unicode bar + line
  output; Kitty / iTerm2 / Sixel image support via `ratatui-image`
- `/Graph Save` to SVG (and plotters PNG output for all chart types)
- `/Data` tree (full): Fill, Sort (with extra keys), Query
  (Find/Extract/Unique/Delete/Modify, F7 repeat), Table 1/2 (F8 repeat),
  Distribution (with Unicode-bar histogram), Regression, Parse, Matrix

**WYSIWYG, Macros, Help**

- R3.4a WYSIWYG icon panel: all 17 icons, mouse-wired, hover hints
- `:` (WYSIWYG) menu: Format (Bold, Color, Alignment), Display (Mode,
  Grid), Special (Copy, Move, Color), Worksheet status; xlsx round-trip
- Macros: `/X` legacy commands; `{BRANCH}`, `{IF}`, `{LET}`, `{PUT}`,
  `{GETLABEL}`, `{GETNUMBER}`, `{MENUBRANCH}`, `{QUIT}`, `{?}` pause,
  `{BEEP}`, special-key tokens, subroutines, `\0` autoexec
- `/Worksheet Learn Range` keystroke recording (Alt-F5 toggle, Alt-F2
  STEP, Alt-F3 RUN)
- F1 context help: full 1-2-3 R3.1 reference manual (824 pages),
  context-aware per mode
- Startup splash screen
- DOS theme (black-on-cyan headers) via `--theme dos`, `L123_THEME`,
  or `theme=` in `~/.l123/L123.CNF`
- Auto-contrast for xlsx cells with light fills on dark terminals

## ✦ Coming

- **M11** `/File Import Json|Jsonl|Parquet|Sqlite` — modern data
  loaders with type inference; `/Range Compare` for diffing two ranges
- **M12** `/Data External` — live SQL backing ranges (SQLite, Postgres)
  with `/DEC Connect`, `/DEU Use`, `/DER Refresh`; xlsx persistence of
  the binding
- **M13** Alt-F10 ADDIN — built-in Data Workbench overlay with a
  VisiData-inspired transform stack (Sort, RegexFilter, Frequency,
  Describe) and value write-back
- Stretch: LMBCS compose key (Alt-F1), additional CRT themes (green,
  amber, classic blue-on-black), APP1/APP2/APP3 plug-in slots

---

## ✦ Architecture

Rust workspace, strict layering:

```
l123-core  ← types only, zero external deps
  ↑
l123-parse, l123-menu
  ↑
l123-engine           (wraps IronCalc behind a trait)
  ↑
l123-cmd, l123-io, l123-graph, l123-print
  ↑
l123-ui               (ratatui + crossterm; engine-agnostic)
  ↑
l123                  (binary)
```

IronCalc is behind the `Engine` trait so it can be swapped. 1-2-3 formula
syntax (`@SUM`, `..`, `#AND#`) is translated to Excel syntax in
`l123-parse` before it reaches the engine. The UI never sees IronCalc
types.

---

## ✦ Authenticity contract

l123 makes two promises (`docs/SPEC.md` §1):

1. An experienced 1-2-3 R3.4a user can drive l123 cold, without reading
   anything.
2. Files round-trip cleanly to and from `.xlsx`.

SPEC §20 enumerates the behaviors — three-line control panel, menu
accelerators, POINT anchor semantics, first-char rule, `@` sigil, format
tags, commit-on-arrow, WYSIWYG icon panel, and so on — that the project
fails if it misses. Every item in the contract has at least one
acceptance transcript under `tests/acceptance/`.

---

## ✦ Development

Strict red / green / refactor. Conventions live in [`CLAUDE.md`](CLAUDE.md).

```bash
cargo test --workspace                                  # all tests
cargo test -p l123-ui --test acceptance                 # keystroke transcripts
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings   # lint
cargo fmt --all                                         # format
```

Acceptance transcripts are `.tsv` files describing keystrokes in and
screen state out; see `tests/acceptance/README.md` for the directive
syntax. Every UI-visible change lands with a transcript.

Canonical docs (treat as sources of truth):

- [`docs/SPEC.md`](docs/SPEC.md) — what l123 *is*
- [`docs/PLAN.md`](docs/PLAN.md) — milestones and risk register
- [`docs/MENU.md`](docs/MENU.md) — the complete menu tree

If code and doc disagree, fix the doc first.

---

## ✦ Non-goals

- Not a DOS emulator. No INT21h, no code pages. Strings are UTF-8.
- Not a visual homage. Functional fidelity, not CRT nostalgia. (Green /
  amber themes are a stretch goal, not the point.)
- Not a macro player for existing `.WK3` files. Read-only `.WK3` import
  is a stretch goal; write is not planned.
- Not a reimplementation of the 1-2-3 compute core. IronCalc does that.
- Not aimed at Lotus 1-2-3 for Windows or SmartSuite. Release 3.4a for
  DOS only.

---

## ✦ Philosophy

Spreadsheets didn't get worse — they just got heavier.

l123 brings back the speed, clarity, and keyboard-driven precision of
early spreadsheet software, without sacrificing compatibility with modern
workflows.

---

## ✦ Why?

Because the `/` key was never the problem.

---

# Starquake

A mobile clone of [Starquake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Starquake_(video_game)) (1985, Stephen Crow) built with libGDX.

The original was a ZX Spectrum 48K arcade-adventure where BLOB (Bio-Logically Operated Being) descends into a destabilized planet to reassemble its core. The defining mechanic: BLOB cannot jump — instead, it lays temporary crumbling platforms to navigate a 512-room underground world.

## Game Overview

- **512 flip-screen rooms** in a 16x32 open-world grid
- **No jumping** — build temporary platforms to traverse gaps and reach higher ground
- **9 randomized core pieces** to collect and deliver each playthrough
- **4-item FIFO inventory** with Cheops Pyramid trading system
- **15 teleporters** with 5-character codes for fast travel
- **Hover pads** for flight sections, **vacuum tube lifts** for vertical movement
- **3 resource bars** (energy, ammo, platforms) and 4 lives
- Enemies scale in difficulty with depth; several instant-kill hazard types

## Project Structure

```
Starquake/
├── research/               # Game design docs and extracted reference assets
│   ├── game-overview.md          # Story, history, reception
│   ├── gameplay-mechanics.md     # Core loop, controls, resources, scoring
│   ├── enemies-and-hazards.md    # Enemy types, static hazards, difficulty scaling
│   ├── map-and-levels.md         # World structure, room types, tile hierarchy
│   ├── items-and-trading.md      # Items, inventory, Cheops Pyramid trading
│   ├── teleporter-codes.md       # All 15 codes per platform version
│   ├── platform-differences.md   # ZX Spectrum / C64 / Atari ST / etc.
│   ├── technical-reference.md    # Specs, memory map, data formats
│   ├── graphics-pipeline.md      # Asset enhancement strategy and tools
│   ├── sprite-extraction.md      # How to extract graphics from the ROM
│   ├── asset-catalog.md          # Full catalog of extracted assets + rendering guide
│   ├── resources.md              # External links, maps, disassemblies
│   └── assets/                   # Extracted graphics from ZX Spectrum ROM
│       ├── tiles/                    # ~120 platform tiles (4x scale)
│       ├── sprites/                  # 44 sprite frames + colored BLOB sheets
│       ├── font/                     # 88 font characters (8x8 native)
│       ├── ui/                       # Border corners, laser variants
│       ├── big_platforms/            # 128 composed 2x2 tile groups
│       ├── rooms/                    # 64 pre-rendered rooms + full minimap
│       ├── starquake.z80             # ZX Spectrum snapshot
│       └── starquake_memory.bin      # Raw 64KB memory dump
└── tools/
    └── extract_graphics.py       # Asset extraction script
```

## Build & Run

### Desktop

```bash
./gradlew :desktop:run
```

### Android

```bash
./gradlew :android:installDebug     # install debug build on connected device
./gradlew :android:assembleRelease  # signed release APK/AAB for Play Store
```

### iOS

RoboVM's bundled libimobiledevice does not support iOS 17+, so use Apple's `xcrun devicectl` for install/launch on modern devices.

**Development build** (sideload to your phone/iPad with the `Starquake Dev` profile):

```bash
./gradlew :ios:build     # produces ios/build/robovm.tmp/Starquake.app
xcrun devicectl device install app --device <udid> ios/build/robovm.tmp/Starquake.app
xcrun devicectl device process launch --console --terminate-existing \
    --device <udid> northern.captain.starquake.ios
```

`--console` streams stdout/stderr (including Java stack traces) back to the terminal. Drop it if the launch tunnel hangs on a particular device.

**Simulator**:

```bash
./gradlew :ios:launchIPadSimulator    # or :ios:launchIPhoneSimulator
```

**Distribution IPA for App Store Connect** — MUST use the `-Pios.dist=true` flag, otherwise the build uses the Dev profile (get-task-allow=true, Apple Development cert) which App Store Connect rejects with `ERROR ITMS-90164` / HTTP 409 "Missing code-signing certificate":

```bash
./gradlew :ios:createIPA -Pios.dist=true
# → ios/build/robovm/Starquake.ipa  (signed with Starquake Dist profile)
```

Verify the embedded profile is the dist one before uploading:

```bash
unzip -p ios/build/robovm/Starquake.ipa Payload/Starquake.app/embedded.mobileprovision \
    | security cms -D | plutil -p - | grep -E '"Name"|get-task-allow'
# expected:
#     "get-task-allow" => false
#   "Name" => "Starquake Dist"
```

Then upload via Transporter.app or `xcrun altool --upload-app -f ios/build/robovm/Starquake.ipa`.

The signing identity + profile selection lives in `ios/build.gradle`.

## Asset Extraction

All graphics were extracted directly from the ZX Spectrum ROM. No pre-existing sprite rips exist online for Starquake.

```bash
python -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
pip install Pillow skoolkit
python tools/extract_graphics.py research/assets/starquake.z80
```

## Reference Versions

| Purpose | Version | Why |
|---------|---------|-----|
| Gameplay & data | ZX Spectrum | Original; most documented; disassemblies available |
| Visual inspiration | C64 / Atari ST | Best-looking 8-bit and 16-bit versions |
| Audio inspiration | C64 (SID) | Iconic music composed by Stephen Crow |

## Key References

- [Icemark data format analysis](https://www.icemark.com/dataformats/starquake/index.html) — room/tile data structure
- [Level7 ZX Spectrum disassembly](https://level7.org.uk/miscellany/starquake-disassembly.txt) — annotated Z80 assembly
- [BBC Micro disassembly (GitHub)](https://github.com/reubenscratton/starquake) — full buildable source
- [Complete ZX Spectrum map](https://maps.speccy.cz/map.php?id=Starquake) — 4096x4656 fan-made map
- [TileMap interactive viewer](https://simonowen.com/articles/tilemap/) — technical analysis of room system

# The Tornado Project
## Tools, Add-Ons and Patches

Source: [TornadoMan's Bunker](http://www.moodurian.com/tornado/tor/mods.html)

### Tornado Map Fax Machine (TMF)
[TMF 1.06](TMF106/)

[TMF 1.07](TMF107/) (Version 1.07 Fixes a bug that was introduced in
1.06 an prevented NVG s to work in the Desert Storm scenario)

This allows you to print captured screens of the Tornado Mission Planner
(without having to leave Tornado) on most HP laser/inkjet and EPSON or
NEC 24 needle printers (and compatible printers) as gray-scale maps
(much like a fax, hence the name of the tool). These hardcopies can be
used as maps for the planned missions. This will give you better
orientation during the flight, and you can use a series of maps to
document and analyse the progress of your campaign. Printed maps are
especially helpful when you have to attack (say) an NBC factory with
LGBs but you forgot which of the factory buildings is the NBC
factory. It's also very useful if you have to divert from your
pre-planned route and you need to find a safe way home thru the enemy
air defences (e.g. when short on fuel or after aborting a mission
because of system damage).

#### NVG
Another add-on that comes with TMF is an optional simulation of
night vision goggles (NVGs), helmet mounted devices that enhance the
ambient light at night. You can switch them off and on during flight.

#### TMF's snow
Included in the TMF package is an unofficial patch of Tornado that will
optionally give the impression of a winter landscape in the European
warzones, that is the ground and buildings appear to be covered by snow
and (optionally) some aircraft are painted in winter camo.

### Soundblaster Cannon patch (T_CANNON)
[T_CANNON](T_CANNON/)

Many users of Tornado versions 1.0c - 1.0e have reported problems when
using a Soundblaster SB 16 sound card. Frequently, the computer locks up
after firing the cannon. The only known cure so known until now was to
switch to the ADLIB driver on the PREFERENCES Screen, but this resulted
in slightly less realistic sounds. This is a beta test patch to correct
the problem. It should work with the following versions of Tornado:

- European (DI) versions 1.0c, 1.0d, 10.e
- American Versions 1.0c, 1.0d
- American Versions 1.0d patched with the European 1.0e patch

It will not work with the Trimark Interactive 1.0e Edition of
Tornado. The reason for this is that in the Trimark release,
Soundblaster support was intentionally disabled internally (probably
because of the SB16 problems).

Soundblaster compatibility (or the lack of it) was a problem for Tornado
right from its release. Some versions would not work with any
soundblaster card, but version 1.0c seemed to fix most problems except
for SoundBlaster 16 owners: Firing the cannon could lock your computer
when selecting SoundBlaster as the sound device. The only option for
SB16 users was to switch to the somewhat less dramatic Adlib
sounds. This problem was so bad that some subsequent releases of Tornado
had their entire Soundblaster support disabled for good internally. Even
if you select the SoundBlaster option, the program will automatically
choose the Adlib driver. For those SB16 owners who still have
Soundblaster support in their copy of Tornado and experience the
cannon-lockup-problem, I wrote a little patch that seems to fix the
lock-up problem on most systems.

### Generic Tornado Patcher (TPATCHER)

[TPATCHER](TPATCHER/)

You'll also have to download this Generic Tornado Patcher to use the
cannon patch.

### Action 16 Edition SoundBlaster patch (A16_SB)

[A16_SB](A16_SB/)

The Action 16 edition (mainly sold in Europe) of Tornado is a budget
version that has the Desert Storm extension on it (version 1.0e) and
comes on a CD-ROM, either in a box or in a jewel case with an online
Adobe PDF manual. A similar edition was published as a cover-CD-ROM on
the German language magazine "Bestseller Games Collection" (issue
12). The problem with these versions is that Soundblaster sound effects
were disabled in these editions with the exception of the Quickstart
option where you still can hear digitized sound effects. I've written a
patch that will allow you to hear Soundblaster effects in all parts of
the simulation. Note that this patch will probably not work with the
American Trimark edition that also had it's SB effects disabled.

### The Logbook Editor (TLE12B)

[TLE12B](TLE12B/)

The Tornado Logbook Editor (TLE) is a tiny program to edit almost all
aspects of the Tornado pilot logbooks. Yes, you can actually promote
your pilot!

### A Safer Keyboard Layout (TKM)

[TKM](TKM/)

Tornado Keyboard Mapper is a little memory resident program that will
change the keyboard layout of Tornado. I wrote it after I had (for the
third time) ejected by accident from my Tornado (I wanted to press
CTRL-R to switch off the radar, but actually hit CTRL-E: eject).

### Soundblaster Autodetect patch (T_SBDT)

[T_SBDT](T_SBDT/)

When Tornado was released, a 486-DX-33 was quite a fast machine. Like
many other games, Tornado has problems on some fast machines, especially
with the routines for Sound Blaster autodetection (the program (at least
version 1.0c upwards) ignores the value of the BLASTER environment
variable and tries to find out the correct values for IRQ and port
address by "experimentation", it always uses DMA channel 1, by the way,
and the only IRQ values supported by Tornado are 2,3,5 and 7. If your
soundcard is set to use a different IRQ, it won't work with Tornado
1.0c - 1.0e). On fast machines, this autodetection mechanism sometimes
fails. After you select "TAKE OFF" in the Mission Planner, the cockpit
fails to show up and you are thrown back into the mission planner with a
warning like "soundcard not present". In this case, the patch T_SBDT.ZIP
might be helpful.

### showPT2

[SHOWPT2](SHOWPT2/)

The Review feature of Tornado contains a library of nice pictures of the
different types of aircraft and other vehicles modelled in the
simulation. Those pictures are stored in a file format that seems to be
used only by DI. The program ShowPT2 will convert these pictures to the
BMP Bitmap format, so you can use those pictures for private purposes
like MS Windows wallpaper (and only for private use because those
pictures are (c) by DI !!). This version features optional correction of
the aspect ratio and clipping of black borders around some pictures.

### TCSC (For Windows 3.1/Windows 98)

[TCSC](TCSC/)

Tornado Command and Staff College (TCSC) is a tutorial for Tornado
Command Campaign gameplay, discussing how to survive and win a virtual
campaign in Tornado both from the tactical pilot and the strategic
commander perspective. It was written by Eric Joiner, Basil Copeland and
Heinz-Bernd Eggenstein (that's me).  Unlike many other strategy guides
and FAQ lists, TCSC is not a mere ASCII file, it was written in Windows
3.1 helpfile format, so it has hypertext links, 256-color graphics and
even (optionally) some sound bites.  Discussing TCSC is beyond the scope
and capacity of this website. To learn all about TCSC (and much more),
go to one of the hottest flight sim related sites on the WWW: the TCSC
homepage. TCSC is shareware (US$ 10). In return for the 10 bucks, you'll
also get a password which can be used to decrypt additional goodies:
several hot Tornado add-on programs.

### Tornado Spouse Reminder Tool (TSRT)

[TSRT](TSRT/)

Has this ever happened to you? You fly a really exciting Tornado
mission, evading lots of SAMs and bombing the hell out of those orange
enemies. Suddenly, a complete stranger enters the cockpit, and wants to
talk to you about some irrelevant things like your children, mortgages,
plans for spending weekends together etc. After some time, you realize
this person is not really a complete stranger, she looks familiar
... she's your wife! How embarrassing! During all those hours in the
cockpit, you forgot what she looks like! Now, with this incredible new
tool, the result of months of scientific work by our team of experts,
this can no longer happen to you: We are proud to introduce the Tornado
Spouse Reminder Tool (TSRT). This program allows you to stick a photo of
your spouse to Tornado's front cockpit dashboard!

### Tornado Ordinance Management (T_ORDN)

[T_ORDN](T_ORDN/)

Tornado by DI is supposed to simulate a limited supply of ordnance from
which you have to take configure your Tornados. However, this feature
does not work correctly, making it impossible to run out of ordnance in
even the most costly and long campaign. But there's nothing that can
keep us Tornadoholics from simulating a limited supply of weaponry
independently. This can be tedious if you do it all by pencil and paper,
e.g. counting all the different bombs and missiles loaded to the up to 8
Tornados in a mission can be a pain. To assist in this task, I wrote a
program ORDNANCE.EXE and a simple Excel 3.0 spreadsheet ORDNANCE.XLS
that will help you automate this process a bit. (There's also an
identical spreadsheet file ORDNANCE.wk1 in Lotus-1-2-3 file format)

### TCSC add-on: Desert Storm: Gulf '96 add-on campaign

[TCSC](TCSC/)

This is an encrypted file. Unless you are a registered TCSC user and
have the registration password, don't download it. Gulf '96 is an add-on
campaign and bug-fix package for the "Operation Desert Storm" part of
Tornado (versions 1.0d and 1.0e only). It adds a campaign that is much
harder than the original ODS campaign and fixes some bugs in ODS as
well. This zip file also includes the TORNADO ODS Enhancement Patch.

### Time Compression TSR program (TTC10)

[TTC10](TTC10)

This handy tool allows you to speed up the actual gameplay by N times,
thereby allow you to fast-forward past the "boring" parts of the
mission, and to quickly go to crucial points of the mission. TTC is a
simple TSR that allows time compression during Tornado missions. Time
compression makes events happen faster, and is normally used to quickly
skip "less interesting" parts of a mission. In Tornado, the outcome of a
mission might not always be successful. The mission must be aborted and
repeated unless you want your favorite "pilot" to be forever KIA. If
nothing else is changed a repeated mission will closely resemble the
original. Often this implies a lot of waiting (in real-time) while the
auto-pilot goes from turn-point to turn-point. YOU know that until
way-point so-and-so is reached nothing interesting will happen. And you
will go and make a cup of cofee. But after several retries you sort of
get fed up with making cofee, and you don't really have anything else
(short-term) to do. It gets a bit boring (and time-consuming) to wait
for the action (sorry DI). TTC will reduce the waiting time by a factor
2-8.

### Liberation Campaign (LIBERAT)

[LIBERAT](LIBERAT/)

This is an add-on initial campaign situation for the European Warzone
no. 2. It's meant to be much harder to win than the other campaigns that
come with DI's Tornado, as you start with a disadvantage and because the
enemy is less ambitious.

### Morale Patch (T_MORALE)

[T_MORALE](T_MORALE/)

This unofficial patch fixes a slight bug in the way Tornado calculates
allied and enemy morale during campaigns.

### Terrain Following Realism Patch (T_RIDE_P)

[T_RIDE_P](T_RIDE_P/)

This unofficial patch allows you to fly in TF mode at 100ft AGL (real
MRCA Tornados can do that)! While this will help you evade missiles and
enemy radar, it also has a downside to fly that low: power lines! So be
careful.

### Default Speed Patch (T_DSPEED)

[T_DSPEED](T_DSPEED/)

Another unofficial patch, this one allows you to set the default mission
planner waypoint speed to values higher than 420 kts. Usually, you'd
like the IDS Tornados to cruise at 500+ kts, which is more fuel
efficient than the usual 420 kts for navigation waypoints, as the latter
means you have to accelerate fast to get to 500+ kts for the target
waypoints.

### BDA Patch (TBDA)

[TBDA](TBDA/)

This tool generates ASCII reports of the debriefing texts after a
mission, this is especially useful when doing e-mail campaigns with
others

### Tornado Mission Exchange Tool (TDO_TMX)

[TDO_TMX](TDO_TMX/)

TMX (for short) allows you to refly missions or exchange missions with
others (similar to Red Flag missions in Falcon 3.0). It comes with
several example missions.

### Tornado Joystick Doctor (TJOY_DOC)

[TJOY_DOC](TJOY_DOC/)

This unofficial patch can significantly improve the joystick routines in
Tornado on most machines, especially fast machines (fast by the
standards of Tornado's release time: anything faster than a 486-DX-33!).

### Mission Summary Text Extractor (TDOMISS)

[TDOMISS](TDOMISS/)

This is the first revision of a program to extract a mission summary
from Tornado's .mis and .dta files, listing mission objectives and
waypoints. Copy it to a directory in your path and e.g.

`tdomiss miss1 >miss1.txt`

or

`tdomiss \games\tornado\amp\map5\miss1`

will extract the info for mission 1, to the screen or to disk as
required. Any comments and suggestions gratefully received, particularly
any info on the contents of .dta and .mis files so I can improve the
output. tdomiss has been tested on the missions supplied with 1.0e
Europe. keith.bedford@uk03.bull.co.uk

# Enlarge the AGI heap of Sierra ST AGI 1.422 (SIERRA.PRG). Works on the PRG or on a disk image
# (patches every copy in place, file sizes unchanged).
# patchheap.py <in> <out> [heap_kb]   default 128 (original 64)
# Startup code (text 0x1e24): Malloc(0x7d00 screen + 0x6900 priority + 0x10000 heap).
import sys
src, dst = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]; kb = int(sys.argv[3]) if len(sys.argv) > 3 else 128
assert 64 <= kb <= 4096 and kb % 64 == 0
ctx_old = bytes.fromhex('203c00007d00' '068000006900' '068000010000' '23c0')
ctx_new = ctx_old[:12] + bytes.fromhex('0680') + (kb * 1024).to_bytes(4, 'big') + ctx_old[18:]
d = bytearray(open(src, 'rb').read())
n = d.count(ctx_old); assert n >= 1, 'original bytes not found (already patched?)'
d = d.replace(ctx_old, ctx_new); open(dst, 'wb').write(d)
print('patched %d copies, heap %d KB' % (n, kb))

# Architecture of the native port (`native/`)

The program is plain C++17 + SDL2. There is no Z80 emulation and no translated code: every routine of the original game
(CODE.BIN at 0x7000-0x92FF, MUCODE.BIN at 0x4F00) was rewritten by hand.

## Layout
* `machine.{h,cpp}` - the "hardware": 64 KB RAM image (the original keeps all its data at fixed addresses and the port keeps them),
  CPC video (gate-array palette + mode, recorded per scanline so the original's raster split - mode 0 playfield / mode 1 text area -
  renders correctly), joystick/keyboard, resources (`common/resources.*`: PNG/data/sector files, no .dsk), AY sound chip + firmware sound manager (`sound.*`), the firmware
  services the game used (`Machine::firmware`: palette, keys, disc, events...), the interrupt scheduler and the game task.
* **Interrupts / time.** The original is paced by 6 interrupts per frame. `Machine::runFrame` delivers them at the scanlines of a
  real CPC (`gameIrq` = the game's own handler: phase table, joystick, status-area palette + mode, energy-bar fade, tick counters;
  `fwInterrupt` = firmware: frame-flyback event, ink flash, tickers).
* **The game task.** The game logic is straight-line C++ running as a coroutine (ucontext) started with `Machine::startGame`.
  Wherever the original waited (`halt`, polling a flag set by the interrupt handler, delay loops) it calls `Machine::waitIrq()`
  (`flow::waitTick()`, `flow::timedLoop()` in `port_flow_task.cpp`), which hands control back until the next interrupt.
* `port_*.cpp` - the game, one file per area (see `docs/port_*.md`): `port_flow_*` boot/attract/title/hall of fame/game over,
  `port_game` the in-game loop, `port_player*`, `port_enemy*`, `port_handlers1`, `port_sprite` (XOR sprite engine, collision, animated
  tiles), `port_text` (text, rooms, tiles, disc), `port_sound` (music driver, effects), `port_screen`.
* Routines are registered with `NATIVE(0xADDR, name, "outs", cost) {...}` and called with `Machine::call(addr)`. The original
  address is the routine's identity (it is how the original tables, e.g. entity handlers at 0x937A, refer to them) and the register
  convention of the original is kept (`m.cpu.a`, `hl()`, ... in `regs.h`); `alu.h` has Z80-exact flag helpers for the few places where
  callers look at flags.

## How it was made (and verified)
1. Extract/decrypt the files from the DSK (`tools/extract_assets.py`, `tools/make_resources.cpp`), disassemble (`docs/z80_listing.txt`).
2. A Z80 emulator version (`emu/`) runs the original code with firmware shims.
3. A static Z80->C++ translator (`native/tools/legacy_translator`) produced a bit-identical native version of that code.
4. Every routine was rewritten by hand and checked against the translation: each call was executed natively and by the original on the same
   state and RAM/registers were compared (0 mismatches over many random-input runs and fuzzers), then the translation was deleted.
5. The final assembled program was tested with long random-input runs, the attract mode/demo, name entry and the victory sequence;
   it was not compared bit for bit with the emulator (timing at frame level differs slightly: natives take no CPU time).

## Known differences from the original
* One frame of wrong palette when a game starts; the screen "dissolve" (8E8C) is instant; firmware text output (the "TRICHEZ..."
  message of initiation mode) is not rendered; enemy shots use a xorshift random source (the original read the Z80 R register).
* Not tested at all: the real-time SDL window/audio on a desktop (only headless captures and a dummy-driver start were run).

# C decompilation of `dos/digger.com`

This directory holds a growing, annotated C reconstruction of the original
1983 binary. It is **not** the port in the repository root: the port is the
reference used for names and cross-checks, while every function here is
reconstructed from the 8086 disassembly.

## Conventions

- The `.COM` loads at `CS:0x100`; code addresses are CS:IP values. The
  annotated listing is `../digger.lst`.
- The data segment is at `DS = CS + 0x08E7`; data offsets are DS offsets.
  The data dump is `../digger.dat`.
- The original was compiled with a 16-bit small-model C compiler: `int` is
  16-bit, `long` is 32-bit, pointers are near. This workspace uses fixed-width
  types so it can be read/compiled on a modern machine.
- Names ending in `?` or marked `probable` in `../SYMBOLS.md` are inferred.

rikusw-digger-unix-dos-analysis-md.text:
# `digger.com` vs the C port

This is a reverse-engineering comparison of the original 1983 DOS binary
(`dos/digger.com`) with the C port in this repository.

Artifacts:

- `dos/digger.lst` — full annotated 8086 disassembly, CS:IP addresses.
- `dos/digger.dat` — data-segment hex dump, DS offsets, known tables labelled.
- `dos/SYMBOLS.md` — address/offset symbol tables with confidence levels.
- `dos/CGA.md` — CGA mode/register analysis and DOSBox failure diagnosis.
- `dos/C/` — C decompilation progress (timer/speaker ISR, sound helpers,
  music, levels, CGA, game-state accessors, scoring notes).

## How the binary is organised

- 57,600-byte DOS `.COM`; the loader puts the first file byte at `CS:0x100`.
- It is compiled 16-bit C: stack frames, near pointers, a C runtime argument
  helper at `CS:0x017B`, and the C `ctype` table at `DS:0x509A`.
- The startup sets `DS = SS = CS + 0x08E7`, so:
  - code segment: `CS:0x0100 .. CS:0x8E70` = file `0x0000 .. 0x8D70`;
  - data segment: `DS:0x0000` = file `0x8D70`;
  - `file = CS - 0x100` and `file = DS + 0x8D70`.
- The code segment also contains a few data items (the copyright string at
  `CS:0x8E40`, the saved data segment word at `CS:0x0337`).
- INT 8 is hooked at `CS:0x0339`; the handler starts at `CS:0x0397`.

## Exact data matches

| Table | Original | Port | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8 levels, 150 bytes each | `DS:0x4B0E..0x4FBE` (file `0xD87E..0xDD2E`) | `leveldat[8][10][15]` | **byte-identical** |
| Background jingle | `DS:0x4866`, 291 words | `backgjingle[291]` | **byte-identical** |
| Death jingle (`dirge`) | `DS:0x4AAC`, 49 words | `dirge[]` | **byte-identical** |
| Bonus jingle `T1` | `DS:0x45E4`, 86 words | `bonusjingle[0..85]` | **identical** |
| Bonus jingle `T2` | `DS:0x4700`, 179 words | `bonusjingle[142..320]` | **identical** |
| Core UI strings | `DS:0x4FBE` onward | string literals in `main.c` etc. | **identical** |

The original stores the levels as eight separate arrays, selected by a switch
in `getlevch`; the port stores one contiguous `leveldat` array. The bytes are
the same.

### Bonus jingle and the embedded score block

The original bonus music is not contiguous:

```
DS:0x45E4  T1: 86 words (43 notes)
DS:0x4690  default high-score block: 112 bytes
DS:0x4700  T2: 179 words (89 notes, ends with 0x7D64)
```

The port's `bonusjingle` is `T1` + a **56-word bridge** + `T2`. The bridge
(port indices `86..141`) is not in the binary; it replaces the span occupied
by the original's embedded score block. `T1` and `T2` themselves match exactly.

The embedded score block decodes exactly with the port's `.sco` format:

```
's' + 10 entries of [3-byte initials][2 bytes][6-digit score]
```

The first entry is blank initials with score `1200`; the other nine are `"..."`/
`0`. The port uses the same file format (`scores.c:loadscores`), but does not
embed the 1200 default: with no `.sco` file it starts from zeros.

### Music timing

The effective `soundint` rate is 72.8 Hz. `sett0` (`CS:0x7DD9`) stores
`4*t0val` in the ISR accumulator at `DS:0x024A` (or `0xFFFF` for
`t0val >= 0x3E80`); the timer-0 IRQ rate is `1,193,181/t0val`, so the 16-bit
accumulator overflows `4*1,193,181/65,536 ≈ 72.8` times per second. The port
stores `t0val` and subtracts `0x4000` from the 16-bit accumulator after each
carry in `newsnd.c:getsample()`, which also yields
`1,193,181/16,384 ≈ 72.8 Hz`. Measured on the port: 360 calls in 5 s (72.0 Hz).

At 72.8 Hz:

| Tune | Notes | Duration |
|---|---:|---:|
| original `T1` | 43 | 5.4 s |
| original `T2` | 89 | 12.4 s |
| port's merged bonus jingle | 160 | 21.1 s |

The port's bonus mode lasts `250 - 20*level` frames; the matching original
constant has not been located yet. `T1` is short enough that, depending on the
original's frame rate, it may reach the embedded score block; the music player
would then read the score text as note/duration data. The port's bridge/`T2`
extends the music to 21.1 s, which still outlasts the port's bonus mode, so that
part is normally inaudible. Locating the original's bonus timer is an open
item.

## Exact code matches

### Timer/speaker ISR — `CS:0x0397`

The original handler:

- loads `DS/ES` from `cs:[0x337]`;
- mode `[0x248] == 0`: nothing;
- mode `1`: PWM pulse — sets speaker on, busy-loops `[0x24F]` times, speaker
  off;
- otherwise: toggles the speaker bit on port `0x61`;
- adds `[0x24A]` to `[0x24C]`; on 16-bit carry, increments `[0x24E]` and calls
  `soundint`;
- sends EOI (`0x20` to port `0x20`) and `iret`s.

This is the same model emulated by `newsnd.c` (`getsample`, `pwlut`, `lut`).
The original's PWM is a CPU busy-loop; the port approximates its duration with
timer ticks.

### `soundint` — `CS:0x7227`

The call sequence is exactly the port's:

```
musicupdate
soundemeraldupdate, soundwobbleupdate, soundddieupdate, soundbreakupdate,
soundgoldupdate, soundemupdate, soundexplodeupdate, soundfireupdate,
soundeatmupdate, soundfallupdate, sound1upupdate, soundbonusupdate
then setsoundt2 / setsoundmode+sett0, then sett2val
```

### Sound hardware helpers

The sound-control layer was decompiled and matches the port:

- `sett0` (`CS:0x7DD9`): writes the timer-0 divisor `t0val`, clamps `t0val` to
  1000 for wavetypes 1/2, sets the ISR accumulator (`4*t0val` or `0xFFFF`),
  clamps `musvol` to 1..50, stores `pulsewidth = musvol`, and calls
  `setsoundmode`.
- `setsoundt2` (`CS:0x7E7C`) and `setsoundmode` (`CS:0x7EB8`): same state
  flags (`spkrmode`, `soundt0flag`) and port `0x61` speaker-gate writes.
- `sett2val` (`CS:0x7FA2`) and `timer2` (`CS:0x7FD5`): write the timer-2
  divisor to port `0x42`.
- `startint8` (`CS:0x7EFF`) / `stopint8` (`CS:0x7F36`): hook/restore INT 8 and
  program timer 0. `soundoff` (`CS:0x7CC9`, probable) clears the speaker gate
  and sets timer 0 to `0xFFFF`; `initsound` (`CS:0x7D10`, probable) performs
  the same state initialisation as the port.

### Music — `CS:0x7A70` and `CS:0x7B02`

`music(tune)` sets the same state and the same three envelope parameter sets as
the port. `musicupdate` has the same attack/decay/release state machine and the
same duration multipliers (`*3`, `*6`, `*10`) and `0x7D64` sentinel. The three
table bases are `DS:0x45E4`, `DS:0x4866`, `DS:0x4AAC` — bonus `T1`, background
jingle, dirge.

### Individual sounds

- `soundemerald` (`CS:0x76F7`): same eight frequencies
  (`0x8E8, 0x7F0, 0x712, 0x6AC, 0x5F2, 0x54C, 0x4B8, 0x474`), duration 7,
  state 0, flag 1.
- `soundddie` (`CS:0x7933`): state 0, value 20000, flag 1.
- Score event wrappers at `CS:0x68A2/0x68B0/0x68BE/0x68CC/0x68DA` add
  250/25/250/500/1000. These match the port's `scorekill`, `scoreemerald`,
  `scoreoctave`, `scoregold`, and `scorebonus`. The port's simultaneous
  `scorekill2` (125+125) is an addition.
- The extra-life step uses `0x4E20` (20000), matching the port's
  `bonusscore`.

### `getlevch` — `CS:0x8001`

The original switches on levels 1..8 and returns
`levelData[level-1][y*15 + x]`, with each level in its own 150-byte array.
The port's `leveldat` flattening is equivalent.

### Game-state utilities — `CS:0x8A32..CS:0x8B55`

The high-call-count region is the core state layer and matches the port:

- `incpenalty` (`CS:0x8A32`, 52 callers) increments `DS:0x5014`; this is the
  port's `incpenalty()`.
- `levno` (`CS:0x8ABD`) returns the level at `DS:0x4FE2 + 8*curplayer`.
- `levplan` (`CS:0x8A65`) calls `levno` and applies `(l&3)+5` for `l>8`.
- `levof10` (`CS:0x8A8D`) returns `min(level,10)`.
- `getlives` (`CS:0x8AF0`) and `addlife` (`CS:0x8B0C`) read/increment the two
  lives fields at `DS:0x4FE0`/`DS:0x4FE8`; `addlife` calls `drawlives`.
- The `curplayer` getter (`CS:0x8B45`), probable `nplayers` getter
  (`CS:0x8B4D`), and `testpause` (`CS:0x8B55`) match the port's state access
  and pause flow.

### CGA video — `CS:0x03F4..0x05EB`, `CS:0x1128/0x1155`

The original uses **standard CGA mode 4** (320×200, 4 colours, 2 bpp,
interleaved) but enters it by direct register writes, not INT 10h:

```
3D8h = 02h
CRTC R0..R13 = 38 28 2C 0A 7F 06 64 70 02 01 20 00 00 00
3D9h = 20h
fill 16KB framebuffer with colour 0
3D8h = 0Ah
```

The only nonstandard timing value is the **PCjr H-sync `R2=0x2C`** (IBM CGA
mode 4 uses `0x2D`); the game also rewrites `R2` at runtime (0x2A..0x2E) for
a horizontal shift. The framebuffer address formula is
`(y&~1)*40 + (y&1)*0x2000 + (x>>2)`, i.e. the standard CGA even/odd bank
layout. `R9=1` is normal for mode 4. The startup wrapper `CS:0x03F4` probes
`B800`, enters mode 4, and prints the `DS:0x0263`/`0x0322` message through
the BIOS INT 10h teletype (`CS:0x0456`, gated on the equipment word).
Block/line drawing: `0x0628` (replace) and `0x0655` (XOR) both call the
Bresenham worker `0x0682` through `0x05B0`. The archive's working DOSBox
configuration resolves the display issue; see `dos/CGA.md`.

### Random numbers — `CS:0x177F`

The original has one shared generator for the game and the sound engine:

```
seed = ++DS:0x0DA7;
tick = byte at 0x40:0x006C;            (BIOS timer low byte)
r    = DS:0x0CA7[(seed + tick) & 0xFF];  (256-byte permutation table)
return (r * (n + 1)) >> 8;
```

Call sites: `domonsters` (`randno(15-levof10())`), `monai`
(`randno(levof10()+5)`), and `soundfireupdate` (the t2 jitter). The port's
`randno`/`randnos` 32-bit LCG (`0x15A4E35`) and separate seeds are a
replacement; its sequence differs. See `dos/C/rng.c`.

### Main game loop — `CS:0x86F1`

`game()` is entered **once per life/level** and runs an internal frame loop;
it does not return each frame:

- copy-protection re-check (`DS:0x5016` must be `0x45`, else hang);
- if `levnotdrawn` (`DS:0x5010`) is set: `drawscreen`; if the banner flag
  (`DS:0x5012`) is set, build `"PLAYER n"` at `DS:0x4FEE`, clear the top
  line, flash it in colours 1/2/3 fifteen times, then `addscore(0)`;
  otherwise `initchars` (a re-entry after a death on the same field);
- frame loop: `readdir`, `dodigger`, `domonsters`, `dobags`, penalty delay
  `(8-penalty)*5` or `incmont(penalty-8)`, `testpause`, `checklevdone`;
- on death/level end: `erasediggers`, `musicoff`, a 20-frame bag-settle loop
  (`getnmovingbags`, `dobags`/`dodigger`/`domonsters`), then `playmusic(0)`,
  `killfire`, `erasebonus`, `cleanupbags`, `savefield`, `erasemonsters`,
  `soundlevdone`, level advance on `countem()==0` or `levdone`, life loss
  and `gameover` (`0x610B`) when the last life goes.

`domonsters` loops six monsters (stride `0x28`, table `DS:0x3B1C`), applies
`hnt > 10-levof10()`, and calls `monai` (`CS:0x2E75`), which contains the
port's `randno(levof10()+5)==1` direction swap. `initlevel` (`CS:0x89A4`),
`drawscreen` (`CS:0x89CD`), `initchars` (`CS:0x89E4`), and `initscores`
(`CS:0x5DE0`) map to the port. The post-level path matches the port's
`getnmovingbags` loop plus the soundstop/erasebonus/cleanupbags/savefield/
erasemonsters/countem sequence. `game()` is reconstructed in `dos/C/game.c`.

  y `0x3FE0`, h `0x3FE2`, v `0x3FE4`, rx `0x3FE6`, ry `0x3FE8`, mdir `0x3FEA`,

  `0x3FF4`, notfiring `0x3FF6`, rechargetime `0x3FF8`, fx `0x3FFA`,
  fy `0x3FFC`, fdir `0x3FFE`, expsn `0x4000`, deathstage `0x4002`,
  deathbag `0x4004`, emocttime `0x4016`. It calls `drawdig` `0x263F`,
  `updatefire` `0x4A3E`, `drawexplosion` `0x4E66`, `updatedigger` `0x4F07`,

`initbonusmode` (`CS:0x5528`) sets `bonusmode=1`, `erasebonus`, `ginten(1)`,
`bonustimeleft = 250 - levof10()*20` (`DS:0x400E`),
`startbonustimeleft=20` (`DS:0x400C`), and `DS:0x4014=1`. This is exactly the
port's formula. `createbonus` (`CS:0x5510`), `endbonusmode` (`CS:0x5562`), and
`erasebonus` (`CS:0x5575`) match the port's structure.

### Score storage — INT 13h sector 7

There is **no INT 21h** in the binary. `loadscores` (`CS:0x5DED`, file
`0x5CED`) calls `CS:0x028F`:

```
INT 13h AH=2, drive 0, head 0, cylinder 0x27 (39), sector 7, 1 sector
ES:BX = DS:0x0046
```

and parses `'s'` + ten entries of `[3 initials][2 bytes][6 score digits]`
into `DS:0x4134` (initials) and `DS:0x4108` (32-bit scores). `savescores`
(`CS:0x6521`) builds the same 512-byte buffer and uses `CS:0x02B8` (INT 13h
AH=4 verify, then AH=3 write). The port uses a `.sco` file with the same
format.

reference; it is a default/legacy score image. The sector-2 read/check
(`CS:0x0321` / `CS:0x02F3`) is the disk signature / copy-protection check.

## Differences

### Port additions

- VGA/EGA graphics (`vgagrafx.c`, `alpha.c`), SDL video/keyboard/timer,
  SoundBlaster/DMA (`newsnd.c`), recordings, INI/command-line options, CGA and
  BIOS-palette paths.
- Gauntlet mode, simultaneous two-player mode, and custom level files.
- The port's `getlevch` adds a simultaneous-mode special case
  (`diggers == 2`, levels 3/4, `(6,9)`/`(8,9)` → `'H'`) and a `levfflag` guard;
  neither is in the original's `getlevch`.
- Port-only text: command-line help, INI keys, `SIMULTANEOUS`, `GAUNTLET`,
  `TWO PLAYER`, `TIME UP`, key names, version/copyright strings.
- The original has `TWO`/`PLAYERS` text, so a two-player option exists, but
  there is no `SIMULTANEOUS` or `GAUNTLET` string; the port's simultaneous mode
  is an extension.

### Behavioral differences

- **RNG**: the original uses the shared table+BIOS-tick generator at
  `CS:0x177F` (256-byte permutation at `DS:0x0CA7`, counter at `DS:0x0DA7`,
  tick byte at `0x40:0x006C`). The port's `randno`/`randnos` use a 32-bit LCG
  with multiplier `0x15A4E35` and separate seeds; that constant is not in the
  binary, so the port's random sequence differs. On SDL `getlrt()` returns 0,
  making the port's sequence deterministic.
- **PWM emulation**: the original's mode-1 pulse is a CPU busy-loop whose
  length depends on CPU speed (hence `calibrate()`/`getkips()`); the port
  approximates it with `pwlut` and the sample-level `getsample` model, plus the
  speaker filter/oversampling added for SDL.
- **Score storage**: the original saves high scores in raw disk sector 7
  (INT 13h); the port uses a `.sco` file with the same 512-byte format and
  starts at zeros if the file is absent. The embedded 1200-score block at
  `DS:0x4690` is a default/legacy image with no direct code reference.
- **CGA startup text**: the messages are at `DS:0x0263` / `DS:0x0322`
  (`file 0x8FD3` / `0x9092`; the printable text starts at file `0x9005` /
  `0x90C4`). They are printed via INT 10h after the custom CRTC is installed;
  the SDL port does not have them.

## Open items / next work

- Nothing required.  Optional polish: expand `FUNCTIONS.md` with non-call
  entry points (jump-table targets) and add higher-level animation metadata on
  top of the extracted sprite frames.
- The DOSBox display issue is resolved; see `dos/CGA.md`.

## Method

`objdump -b binary -m i8086 -D -M intel --adjust-vma=0x100
--stop-address=0x8e70 dos/digger.com` produced the code listing; data tables
were located by searching for the port's arrays and by following the
disassembly's DS-relative references. Capstone 5.0.7 was used for targeted
disassembly. Cross-checks used the matching C port as a naming reference, not
as a source of truth: every claim above is backed by bytes in the binary.

## C runtime helpers

The compiler's support routines in the high code region are now named:

| Address | Name | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `CS:0x0172` | `__exit` | restores SP from `DS:0x0000` and far-returns to DOS |
| `CS:0x017B` | `parse_cmdline` | fills the argv array at `DS:0x0004` |
| `CS:0x0227` | `iabs` | integer absolute value |
| `CS:0x080F5` | `digit_value` | `'1'..'9'` → 1..9, otherwise 0 |
| `CS:0x08155` | `toupper_c` | lowercase to uppercase |
| `CS:0x08BFC` | `lmul` | signed 32×32 → low 32 bits |
| `CS:0x08C6D` | `exit_process` | pushes the status and tails into `__exit` |
| `CS:0x08C7D` | `ldivmod` | signed 32/32, quotient + remainder |
| `CS:0x08D2D` | `strcpy_ds` | data-segment `strcpy` |
| `CS:0x08D4C` | `ultoa` | unsigned long to decimal with a field width |
| `CS:0x08DDD` | `inportb` | port read |
| `CS:0x08DE8` | `outportb` | port write |
| `CS:0x08DF4` | `strcat_ds` | data-segment `strcat` |
| `CS:0x08E23` | `lcmp` | signed 32-bit compare |

Reconstructed in `dos/C/runtime.c`; the ABI notes are in its header.

## Tooling

- `dos/FUNCTIONS.md` is generated by `dos/tools/label_functions.py`.  It lists
  every CALL target in `digger.lst` (plus the entry point and the INT 8/INT 9
  handlers), with the file offset and the first instruction; unlabeled
  boundaries are `loc_XXXX`.
- `dos/tools/compare_tables.py` extracts the reconstructed C tables and
  byte-compares them with `dos/digger.com`: the eight level arrays, the RNG
  permutation table, the CGA CRTC table and the default sprite draw order.
  It exits non-zero on any mismatch, so it can gate future edits.
- `dos/tools/extract_data.py` extracts all data to `dos/data/`: the complete
  code/data segment images, every table (levels, music, RNG, ctype, scores,
  strings, orders, the keyboard scan-code table, the copyright string), the
  64-glyph font with its dispatch table, all 76 sprite frames as data/mask
  banks plus PNGs, and the title RLE, framebuffer and PNG.  The output is
  deterministic and ignored by git (`dos/data/`); only the tool and the
  generated-format description are committed.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
dott_save_convert.py - convert a Day of the Tentacle Remastered save (Steam/GOG, savegame.NNN)
into a save file for the original 1993 DOS interpreter (TENTACLE.EXE, CD version), e.g. for
DOSBox, a real PC, or the MiSTer ao486 core with the 0MHz collection.

No dependencies. Python 3.8+.

    python dott_save_convert.py savegame.001 SAVEGAME.002 --donor donor-dos-save.bin --name "Steam save"

The "donor" is any save written by the DOS interpreter itself (start a new game, save in any
slot, take SAVEGAME.0NN). It supplies two small engine-specific parts that the Remaster stores in
a different layout: the transient "verbs / local objects / sentence queue" block and the iMUSE
sound-driver state. Both are rebuilt by the game as soon as you change room or a tune starts, so
any donor works. A start-of-game donor is bundled with the tool.

Format notes (reverse-engineered 2026-09, see README.md):
  Remaster file  = 352-byte Double Fine wrapper + classic SCUMM v6 save block + zero padding
  classic block  = 'SAVE' BE32 len | 'VARS' BE32 len | ver 03 00 | name[32] | engine header |
                   actors | object owner/state[800] | class table[800*4] | vars[800*2] |
                   bitvars[256] | transient block | 'SNDD' chunk | GLOB heap | 'USED' list
  DOS differences: class table written twice; array/name/verb-string heap blocks use 16-bit
                   header fields (Remaster: 32-bit); scale tables have 200 entries (Remaster 400);
                   heap type 16 (object names) does not exist; USED list ends with FF FF (not 00 00).
"""
import argparse
import struct
import sys

VARS_COUNT = 800            # DOTT MAXS
BITVARS_BYTES = 2048 // 8
CLASS_TABLE_BYTES = 800 * 4
NAME_OFF = 0x12
NAME_LEN = 32


def be32(b, o):
    return struct.unpack_from(">I", b, o)[0]


def le16(b, o):
    return struct.unpack_from("<H", b, o)[0]


def le32(b, o):
    return struct.unpack_from("<I", b, o)[0]


def find_classic_block(data):
    """Return (offset, length) of the classic 'SAVE' block inside a Remaster or DOS file."""
    for off in (0, 352):
        if data[off:off + 4] == b"SAVE" and data[off + 8:off + 12] == b"VARS":
            return off, be32(data, off + 4)
    i = data.find(b"SAVE")
    while i >= 0:
        if data[i + 8:i + 12] == b"VARS":
            return i, be32(data, i + 4)
        i = data.find(b"SAVE", i + 1)
    raise ValueError("no SCUMM 'SAVE' block found")


def find_vars(c):
    """Locate the 800-entry variable array using three constant key-code variables
    (VAR_CUTSCENEEXIT_KEY=27 at index 24, VAR_PAUSE_KEY=32 at 43, VAR_MAINMENU_KEY=319 at 50)."""
    for p in range(16, len(c) - 2 * VARS_COUNT):
        if le16(c, p + 48) == 27 and le16(c, p + 86) == 32 and le16(c, p + 100) == 319:
            return p
    raise ValueError("could not locate the variable array (not a DOTT save?)")


def split_regions(c):
    """Offsets of the regions we care about, for a block in either layout."""
    vars_off = find_vars(c)
    snd = c.find(b"SNDD")
    if snd < 0:
        raise ValueError("no SNDD chunk")
    snd_len = be32(c, snd + 4)
    heap = snd + snd_len
    return {
        "vars": vars_off,
        "class": vars_off - CLASS_TABLE_BYTES,
        "transient": vars_off + 2 * VARS_COUNT + BITVARS_BYTES,
        "sndd": snd,
        "sndd_len": snd_len,
        "heap": heap,
    }


def is_dos_layout(c):
    """DOS saves carry the class table twice: the 3200 bytes before the vars equal the 3200 before that."""
    r = split_regions(c)
    a = c[r["class"]:r["vars"]]
    b = c[r["class"] - CLASS_TABLE_BYTES:r["class"]]
    return a == b


def walk_globs(c, p):
    """Yield (offset, total, alloc, type, index) for each GLOB block starting at p."""
    while p + 16 <= len(c) and c[p:p + 4] == b"GLOB":
        total = be32(c, p + 4)
        yield p, total, le32(c, p + 8), le16(c, p + 12), le16(c, p + 14)
        p += total


def glob(total, alloc, typ, idx, payload):
    out = bytearray(b"GLOB")
    out += struct.pack(">I", total) + struct.pack("<IHH", alloc, typ, idx) + payload
    out += b"\0" * (total - len(out))
    return bytes(out)


def convert_heap(c, heap_off, drop_types=(16,), log=None):
    """Rewrite the GLOB heap + USED list from Remaster form to DOS form."""
    out = bytearray()
    p = heap_off
    for off, total, alloc, typ, idx in walk_globs(c, heap_off):
        data = c[off + 16:off + total]
        tag = data[:4]
        is_resource = len(tag) == 4 and all(65 <= x <= 90 for x in tag)
        if typ == 11 and len(data) == 400:
            # scale table: Remaster keeps 400 entries (doubled vertical space), DOS 200
            payload = bytes(data[0:400:2])
            out += glob(216, 208, typ, idx, payload)
            if log: log(f"t11#{idx}: scale table 400 -> 200")
        elif typ in drop_types:
            if log: log(f"t{typ}#{idx}: dropped (type unknown to the DOS interpreter)")
        elif typ in (7, 8, 9, 16) and not is_resource:
            # array / name / verb-string block: 3 x uint32 header -> 3 x uint16
            kind, d1, d2 = struct.unpack_from("<III", data, 0)
            if max(kind, d1, d2) > 0xFFFF:
                raise ValueError(f"t{typ}#{idx}: header is not the 32-bit Remaster form")
            body = data[12:]
            real = d1 * d2 * (2 if kind == 5 else 1)
            real = min(real, len(body))
            payload = struct.pack("<HHH", kind, d1, d2) + body[:real]
            nalloc = ((len(payload) + 7) // 8) * 8 + 8
            out += glob(nalloc + 8, nalloc, typ, idx, payload)
            if log: log(f"t{typ}#{idx}: {total} -> {nalloc + 8} bytes (16-bit header)")
        else:
            out += c[off:off + total]
        p = off + total
    if c[p:p + 4] != b"USED":
        raise ValueError("expected USED list after the heap")
    # USED: 'USED' BE32 total | LE32 alloc | LE16 12 | LE16 1 | entries (LE16 type, LE16 idx, u8 flags) | terminator
    q = p + 16
    entries = bytearray()
    while q + 5 <= len(c):
        t = le16(c, q)
        if t == 0 or t == 0xFFFF:
            break
        entries += c[q:q + 5]
        q += 5
    utotal = 16 + len(entries) + 2
    out += b"USED" + struct.pack(">I", utotal) + struct.pack("<IHH", utotal - 8, 12, 1) + entries + b"\xff\xff"
    if log: log(f"USED: {len(entries) // 5} resources, FFFF terminator")
    return bytes(out)


def convert(remaster_bytes, donor_bytes, name, log=None):
    off, length = find_classic_block(remaster_bytes)
    c = bytes(remaster_bytes[off:off + length])
    if is_dos_layout(c):
        raise ValueError("input already has the DOS layout (class table twice); nothing to convert")
    r = split_regions(c)
    doff, dlen = find_classic_block(donor_bytes)
    d = bytes(donor_bytes[doff:doff + dlen])
    if not is_dos_layout(d):
        raise ValueError("donor is not a save written by the DOS interpreter")
    dr = split_regions(d)

    out = bytearray()
    out += c[:r["vars"]]                                   # header, actors, owner/state, class table
    out += c[r["class"]:r["vars"]]                         # class table again (DOS quirk)
    out += c[r["vars"]:r["transient"]]                     # vars + bitvars
    out += d[dr["transient"]:dr["heap"]]                   # donor's transient block + SNDD chunk
    out += convert_heap(c, r["heap"], log=log)             # heap + USED
    struct.pack_into(">I", out, 4, len(out))               # SAVE length
    vars_len = out.find(b"SNDD") - 8
    struct.pack_into(">I", out, 12, vars_len)              # VARS length
    nm = name.encode("ascii", "replace")[:NAME_LEN - 1]
    out[NAME_OFF:NAME_OFF + NAME_LEN] = nm + b"\0" * (NAME_LEN - len(nm))
    return bytes(out)


def info(data):
    off, length = find_classic_block(data)
    c = data[off:off + length]
    r = split_regions(c)
    layout = "DOS" if is_dos_layout(c) else "Remaster"
    name = c[NAME_OFF:NAME_OFF + NAME_LEN].split(b"\0")[0].decode("ascii", "replace")
    v = lambda i: le16(c, r["vars"] + 2 * i)
    print(f"classic block at {off}, {length} bytes, layout: {layout}, name: '{name}'")
    print(f"  room {v(4)}, ego actor {v(1)}, vars at {r['vars']}, SNDD at {r['sndd']} ({r['sndd_len']} B), heap at {r['heap']}")
    n = 0
    inv = 0
    for _, total, alloc, typ, idx in walk_globs(c, r["heap"]):
        n += 1
        if typ == 5:
            inv += 1
    print(f"  heap: {n} blocks, {inv} inventory objects")


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Day of the Tentacle Remastered -> DOS save converter")
    ap.add_argument("input", help="Remaster savegame.NNN (or any file holding the classic block)")
    ap.add_argument("output", nargs="?", help="DOS save to write, e.g. SAVEGAME.002")
    ap.add_argument("--donor", default=None, help="a save written by the DOS interpreter (default: bundled donor-dos-save.bin)")
    ap.add_argument("--name", default="Converted save", help="name shown in the DOS load dialog (max 31 chars)")
    ap.add_argument("--info", action="store_true", help="only print what the file contains")
    ap.add_argument("-v", "--verbose", action="store_true")
    a = ap.parse_args()

    data = open(a.input, "rb").read()
    if a.info or not a.output:
        info(data)
        return 0
    donor_path = a.donor
    if donor_path is None:
        import os
        donor_path = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "donor-dos-save.bin")
    donor = open(donor_path, "rb").read()
    log = (lambda s: print("  " + s)) if a.verbose else None
    out = convert(data, donor, a.name, log=log)
    open(a.output, "wb").write(out)
    print(f"wrote {a.output} ({len(out)} bytes)")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

# TerraFire port

Native macOS/Windows port of TerraFire (DOS, Owen Thomas) on SDL3. Needs the
original `DATA.PAK` (6,582,958 bytes); the original executables are not used.

## Build

macOS (Homebrew):

    brew install cmake ninja sdl3
    cmake -S . -B build -G Ninja
    cmake --build build                    # -> build/terrafire

A self-contained universal TerraFire.app, as in the releases (SDL3 is
built from source and linked in):

    cmake -S . -B build-app -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DTF_VENDOR_SDL=ON \
          -DTF_MACOS_BUNDLE=ON "-DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64;x86_64"
    cmake --build build-app                # -> build-app/TerraFire.app

Windows (Visual Studio 2022 or newer, from a developer prompt):

    cmake -S . -B build
    cmake --build build --config Release   # -> build/Release/terrafire.exe + SDL3.dll

Or cross-compile for Windows from macOS / Linux with MinGW-w64
(`brew install mingw-w64`):

    tools/package-windows.sh               # -> dist/terrafire-windows.zip

If SDL3 isn't installed, CMake downloads and builds it (`-DTF_VENDOR_SDL=ON`
forces that). The Windows build is a GUI program with no console; configure
with `-DTF_WINDOWS_CONSOLE=ON` to see its log output.
`.github/workflows/build.yml` builds all of these on GitHub Actions, and
pushing a `v*` tag runs `release.yml`, which publishes the Windows and macOS
packages as a GitHub release.

## Run

    build/terrafire [directory containing DATA.PAK]

Without a directory it looks in the current folder, next to the executable,
and (TerraFire.app) in the folder containing the app. Settings and saves are
kept beside DATA.PAK.

    build/terrafire ..                     # the game: splash, title, main menu
    build/terrafire --play ..              # straight into a new game, difficulty 1, mission 1
    build/terrafire --play 0 5 ..          # difficulty 0-3, start at mission 1-27
    build/terrafire --viewer ..            # asset viewer

In the viewer, Left/Right change entry, Up/Down change frame, Shift+arrows
scroll, Enter toggles tile sets / sprite banks, P cycles palettes, Space
plays the next sound, Esc quits.

Controls come from SETTINGS.CFG (default: Left/Right turn, Up thrust, Space
fire; Options > Control > Set Keys changes them), P pauses, Esc opens the
in-game menu, F1 shows the instructions. Gamepads work as the original's
joystick: in a mission the stick (or D-pad) turns and thrusts and A/X fires;
in menus the stick moves and A/X selects; B or Start is Esc. Plugging one in
turns Options > Control > JOYSTICK on.

Options > Graphics also has two port-only settings, kept in PORT.CFG so
SETTINGS.CFG stays in the original's format: FULLSCREEN (desktop fullscreen)
and SCALING. SHARP (default) is the largest 4:3 picture, as on the original
VGA monitor's non-square pixels, drawn with sharp bilinear: scaled up by whole
numbers with no smoothing, then smoothly to the final size, so pixels stay
crisp and even. INTEGER is the largest picture with whole-number pixel sizes
(between square and 4:3, so the shape is only close to 4:3). FILL stretches to
the whole window. Sizes are in real pixels on HiDPI/Retina screens.

Saved games are GAME0001.SAV-GAME0005.SAV next to SETTINGS.CFG, in the
original's format (the DOS game loads them too).

## Testing

Hooks (environment variables): TF_KEYS="frame:code,frame:-code,..." injects
key make/break events, TF_SHOT_PRESENT=n:file.bmp saves the n-th shown frame,
TF_SAVE_TICK=n acts as if a save point were collected at game tick n,
TF_KILL_TICK=n loses the last life at tick n, TF_CHEATS=1 enables F5-F8,
TF_PAD="from-to:x,y,fire,back;..." simulates a gamepad (frames count calls
to the frame presenter, as for TF_KEYS and TF_SHOT_PRESENT).

Self-checks:

    build/terrafire --selftest ..                    # decode every pak entry
    build/terrafire --demo-check ..                  # replay demo input timelines
    build/terrafire --attract 300 ..                 # attract mode, stop after 300 ticks
    build/terrafire --load-mission 0 out.bmp ..      # load a mission's resources and check them
    build/terrafire --object-check ..                # object list, movement and callback rules
    build/terrafire --render-test 0 out.bmp ..       # draw a test scene with the renderer
    build/terrafire --first-frame 1 out.bmp ..       # a demo's real start-up and first frame
    build/terrafire --view-object 3 74 out.bmp ..    # after start-up, centre the view on an object
    build/terrafire --demo-run 3 3000 out.bmp ..     # play a demo for N ticks, report input/heading
    build/terrafire --trace 3 600 port.csv ..        # per-step state trace (see below)
    build/terrafire --screenshot 30 0 out.bmp ..     # render one tile-set frame or sprite to BMP

## Checking against the original

`re/tools/trace_original.py` runs the original PART2.EXE code under the
Unicorn CPU emulator (Python: `pip install unicorn`) and writes the same
per-step trace as `--trace`, so the two can be compared:

    ../re/.venv/bin/python ../re/tools/trace_original.py 3 600 orig.csv ..
    build/terrafire --trace 3 600 port.csv ..
    python3 ../re/tools/trace_compare.py orig.csv port.csv

Reference traces for all four demos, plus demo input replayed on every
mission that has no demo of its own (demo 0 on the bonus missions, demo 3
on the rest; 31 in all), are kept in `re/traces/`; check the port against
all of them with (from the repository root):

    re/tools/regress.sh

`TF_DEMO_MISSION=n` (both tools) replays a demo's input on mission n, and
`TF_INVULNERABLE=1` sets the original's no-collision flag, to test missions
that have no demo.

Only DOS-facing routines are replaced in the emulated run (file I/O,
allocation, clock, vsync, sound, text output); the game logic runs as
compiled. The comparison reports the first frame and field that differ.

A few paths of the original that the game never reaches are not ported; if
one is ever hit, it is logged once (`unported.c`) and counted in the
`--attract` / `--play` summary.

## Layout

- `src/platform.h`, `src/platform_sdl.c`: replaces the DOS hardware: VGA
  framebuffer and palette, int 9 keyboard (XT scancodes), timer, sound,
  gamepads.
- `src/pak.c`: DATA.PAK access (table of contents taken from PART2.EXE).
- `src/assets.c`: palette, DWD sound, tile set and sprite bank decoders.
- `src/viewer.c`: asset viewer (`--viewer`).
- `src/kbd.c`, `src/timing.c`, `src/palette.c`: the original's keyboard
  latches, frame pacing and palette fades; `src/joystick.c` turns a gamepad
  into key presses as the original's joystick code did.
- `src/demo.c`, `src/session.c`: demo input timeline, attract loop, new game,
  session loop, mission start and end. `src/game.h` holds the game state;
  `src/state.c` converts it to and from the original's state block and
  reads/writes SETTINGS.CFG.
- `src/res.c`: the engine's resource tables (frame slots, tile chunks, sprite
  banks with 8 orientation views) and their garbage collector.
- `src/levels.c`: level, bonus-level and HUD loaders, background tile animation.
- `src/objects.c`: the 652-object table, z-sorted active list, animations,
  callback timers and per-frame update.
- `src/render.c`: off-screen buffer, camera and view, occlusion grid, tile and
  sprite drawing (orientations, blending), point/fill/line, the beam effect.
- `src/frame.c`: per-frame routines for each screen mode, starfield, world
  wrap-around.
- `src/spawn.c`: level object setup from the placement map (frame slot 3) and
  all the spawners.
- `src/collision.c`: pixel collision against sprites and tile collision shapes.
- `src/player.c`: player input (the exact 15-query order demos depend on),
  rotation, movement, the per-frame player callback and the request handler.
- `src/hits.c`, `src/weapons.c`, `src/effects.c`, `src/pickups.c`: collisions
  and damage, firing and bullets, explosions and debris, pods and pickups.
- `src/tow.c`: towing physics (the original's x87 code) and the self-destruct.
- `src/enemies.c`, `src/bonus.c`: normal-mission enemies, bosses and level
  machinery; the bonus levels.
- `src/hud.c`, `src/sound.c`: status bar, text and messages; sound effects.
- `src/menu.c`, `src/save.c`, `src/screens.c`: menus and info pages, saved
  games (the original's format), briefing / mission complete / game over /
  high scores / ending / splash / title.
- Generated from PART2.EXE: `src/tables_data.c` (`re/tools/gen_tables.py`:
  trig and random tables, weapon banks, sound table, message texts, key
  names), `src/anims_data.c`, `src/callbacks_data.c`
  (`re/tools/gen_objects.py`) and `src/missions_data.c`
  (`re/tools/gen_missions.py`).

Reverse-engineering notes and tools are in `../re/`.

#!/usr/bin/env python3

import os
import sys
import argparse
import re

HEADING_RE = re.compile(r"^#+ ")

HEADING = ""

def specialchars(x):
    return {
        0x0D : 0,    # skip newline handling
        0x0A : 0,
        0x02 : 0x2A, #bold
        0x04 : 0x2A, #double strike->bold
        0x0F : 0x20, #binding space
        0x13 : 0x2A, #underline->italic
        0x19 : 0x2A, #italic
        0x14 : 0x5E, #superscript
        0x16 : 0x7E, #subscript
        0x18 : 0x7E, #strikethrough
        0x1E : 0,    #inactive soft hyphen: strip
        0x1F : 0x2D  #active soft hyphen
    }.get(x, 0)

def process_dotline(buf):
    """Emit markdown for a buffered dot command line (buf includes the leading dot)."""
    cmd = bytes(buf[1:3]).upper() if len(buf) >= 3 else b''
    if cmd in (b'PA', b'CP'):
        return b'\n---\n'
    return b''

def handleblock(block, textmode=False):
    # block[0] is the length of the block (int)
    # block[2] is the command type
    if block[2] == 0x03: # footnote
        notedata = converttext(block[20:], textmode).replace(b'\n', b'')
        return b'^[' + notedata + b']'
    elif block[2] == 0x04: # endnote
        notedata = converttext(block[20:], textmode).replace(b'\n', b'')
        return b'^[' + notedata + b']'
    elif block[2] == 0x05: # annotation
        annotdata = converttext(block[20:], textmode).replace(b'\n', b'')
        return b'<!-- ' + annotdata + b' -->'
    elif block[2] == 0x06: # comment: strip
        return b''
    elif block[2] == 0x09: # TAB
        return b'    '
    elif block[2] == 0x0B: # end of page
        return b'\n---\n'
    elif block[2] == 0x0E: # index item: strip
        return b''
    elif block[2] == 0x11: # paragraph style
        if block[3] == 0x02: # header
            return b'## '
        elif block[3] == 0x03: # subheading
            return b'### '
        elif block[3] == 0x05: # title
            return b'# '
    return b''

def converttext(data, textmode=False):
    counter = -1
    newline = False
    linetype = 0
    dotline_buf = bytearray()
    outdata = bytearray()
    global HEADING
    while counter < len(data) - 1:
        counter += 1
        # End of file character
        if data[counter] == 0x1A:
            break
        # Extended character
        elif data[counter] == 0x1B:
            outdata.append(data[counter + 1])
            counter += 2
        # Symmetrical sequence: 1Dh special character
        elif data[counter] == 0x1D:
            jump = int.from_bytes(data[counter + 1:counter + 3], byteorder='little')
            if not textmode:
                outdata += handleblock(data[counter + 1:counter + 3 + jump], textmode)
                if len(outdata) > 2:
                    HEADING = outdata.decode("cp437").split(" ", 1)[-1]
            counter += jump + 2
        elif data[counter] < 0x20:    # special formatting characters
            if data[counter] == 0x0D and not newline:
                if linetype == 0:
                    outdata += b'\x0A\x0A'
                elif linetype == 1 and not textmode:
                    outdata += process_dotline(dotline_buf)
                    dotline_buf = bytearray()
                newline = True
                linetype = 0
            elif data[counter] == 0x0C and not textmode: # form feed -> horizontal rule
                outdata += b'\n---\n'
            if not textmode:   # handle formatting for markdown
                c = specialchars(data[counter])
                if c != 0:
                    outdata.append(c)
                if data[counter] in (0x02, 0x04, 0x18):
                    outdata.append(c)   # duplicating ** and ~~
        elif data[counter] < 0x80:    # other characters
            if newline:
                newline = False
                if data[counter] == 0x2E: # dotline
                    linetype = 1
                    dotline_buf = bytearray()
                #if data[counter] == 0x2D: # special line (list)
                #    outdata.pop()
            if linetype == 1:
                dotline_buf.append(data[counter])
            else:
                outdata.append(data[counter])
        elif data[counter] == 0x8D: # soft return (word-wrap line break)
            outdata.append(0x0A)
        elif data[counter] < 0xFF:
            outdata.append(data[counter] - 0x80)
    return outdata

def main():
    global HEADING
    print("Basic WordStar to Markdown converter")
    print("====================================")

    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("ws_file", help="the WordStar file to convert")
    parser.add_argument("-o", "--output", help="output file name")
    parser.add_argument("-t", "--textmode", help="output to unformatted (text) file",
                        action="store_true")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    if args.output:
        outputfile = args.output
    else:
        extension = ".txt" if args.textmode else ".md"
        base, _ = os.path.splitext(args.ws_file)
        outputfile = base + extension

    print("Reading " + args.ws_file)
    with open(args.ws_file, "rb") as infile:
        data = infile.read()

    print("Converting...")
    outdata = converttext(data, args.textmode)

    if HEADING and not args.output:
        outputfile = f"{HEADING.strip()}.md"

    outstring = outdata.decode("cp437")
    with open(outputfile, "wt", newline='\n') as outfile:
        outfile.write(outstring.replace("\x0D", ""))
    print("Conversion ready, " + outputfile + " written!")

if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()
